card.band: 8 h. Builds are slow and there are many independent kernels, so credit accrues kernel by kernel. A frontier agent speeds up a few kernels with SIMD and threading, and a weaker model breaks the equivalence gate.
card.cheat: Skipping work or caching results is closed by random inputs generated at run time and a bit-exact gate. The builds ship no upstream binaries.
card.grading: A hard gate runs the core gtest suite (excluding OCL tests) and hidden bit-exact or tolerance checks on random Mats of many types and sizes. Then the wall-clock median over a fixed kernel set is compared with the base. Reward is 2^u - 1.
card.reference: The speedup comes from the upstream optimized kernels (SIMD and parallel loops), measured on the same CPU. S is the measured ratio.
card.source: https://github.com/opencv/opencv @ head e70c9da (5.0.0 release listed), Apache-2.0
card.task: Ship a history-less snapshot of the core module built with the universal intrinsics and parallel backends disabled. The agent speeds up arithmetic, convert, reduce, LUT, norm, mean and matmul on 8 cores while the module still builds and the API is unchanged.
card.title: OpenCV core arithmetic and reduction kernels speedup

facts.claim: OpenCV 5.0.0 release exists on the opencv/opencv GitHub repo (tag 5.0.0, listed as 'OpenCV 5.0.0', dated '06 Jun'; year not shown on page)
Repository licence is Apache-2.0 (taken from GitHub API spdx in seed; not re-fetched from LICENSE file)
modules/core/test at tag 5.0.0 has 22 .cpp test sources plus headers (39 files total incl. an ocl subdirectory); per-test TEST/TEST_F counts not visible

CV_DISABLE_OPTIMIZATION is a documented CMake switch in the 5.x config reference that disables universal intrinsics, dispatched SIMD code, IPP/Eigen/LAPACK and loop unrolling (so the 'disabled' base is a build flag, not removed code)
The 5.0 docs describe a core parallel backend API (cv::parallel, OPENCV_PARALLEL_PRIORITY_* env vars, setParallelForBackend)
WITH_TBB / WITH_PTHREADS_PF build option names and defaults
Universal intrinsics (cv::v_float32 etc.) documentation in the 5.0 docs
Config reference page (5.x) fetched directly for exact wording and defaults

full_card.band: 8 h tier. Credit accrues per kernel; frontier agent likely speeds a subset (SIMD + threads); weaker model fails equivalence. No dated public evidence found (E0).

Band.why: No dated public evidence; the 8h scope of seven kernel families is plausible for a frontier agent in some trials but unproven.

Build.why: Unprobed; full core and test build is slow and iterative, estimated around 3 days for our reference plus hidden checks.

Fit.why: CPU-only, 8 cores, 16 GB fits; threading must avoid TBB because it is not installable offline.

Hor.why: 8h tier with many independent kernels and build-debug-measure loops is genuinely long-horizon.

Lic.why: Apache-2.0 permits shipping the source and reference in a bundle.

Multi.why: Seven kernel families give per-kernel buckets of credit.

Nov.why: Nearest neighbour S-op-039 at 0.251 is above the 0.15 novelty threshold; its subject is not known to us.

Real.why: Real 91k-star Apache-2.0 library at a tagged release 5.0.0 with real test tree.

Ref.why: Upstream optimized kernels are complete and permissive; speedup measurable on the same CPU.

Seal.why: Reference is public in git history; sealable only with history-less snapshot and with SIMD/dispatch code deleted rather than flagged off.

Surf.why: Existing gtest suite plus runtime-random Mats across types and sizes gives thousands of checks, but gate is mostly pass/fail plus kernel timings, not an unlimited executable oracle.

spike_plan.kill_if: Disabled-build speedup headroom under 1.3x on most kernels, core suite is nondeterministic, or the base cannot be made to compile with the SIMD and dispatch paths removed.
spike_plan.pass_if: Both builds finish within about 45 minutes; default build is at least 2x faster than disabled on at least three of the seven kernels; flag-off recovers less than about 60% of the default speedup; test results are deterministic across two runs.
steps: In a throwaway networked Linux container, clone opencv at e70c9da (5.0.0) without history, configure two builds: default and -DCV_DISABLE_OPTIMIZATION=ON, both with core and opencv_test_core only, and time each build.
Run opencv_test_core --gtest_filter=-*OCL* on both builds and record pass/fail counts and runtime; repeat once to check determinism.
Write a small benchmark for arithm (add/mul), convertTo, sum/mean/norm, LUT, and gemm on 8 cores; run the median of 5 for default vs disabled builds.
Check whether the flag alone recovers most of the default-build speedup. If it does, the snapshot must delete the dispatch/intrinsic sources, not only flag them off, or the task is one-lever (K10).
Confirm the removed-source variant still compiles and the core tests run on it, and record which tests fail because intrinsics are gone (these must be excluded from the hard gate).

v1.summary: OpenCV 5.0.0 is a real, Apache-2.0 release with a sizeable core test tree and a measurable upstream speedup, so the seed is viable as an 8h optimization task. The main risk is that CV_DISABLE_OPTIMIZATION is a build flag upstream, so the base must delete the SIMD and dispatch paths or the task collapses to one lever; the spike must measure flag-off headroom and build time before commitment.

v2.note: Many independent kernels (arithm, convert, reduce, LUT, norm, mean, gemm) give honest per-lever credit, and S can be measured from the upstream build. Risks the spike must clear: (1) the base must delete the dispatch/.simd.hpp and intrinsic paths from source, not just set CV_DISABLE_OPTIMIZATION, or it becomes one-lever restore-the-flag (K10); (2) removing hal/intrin headers from core may break compilation widely, which drives build cost up; (3) reductions need tolerance, not bit-exact, because accumulation order differs; (4) lock build flags so -O3/-march tweaks are not the lever. No smoke build, and the config-reference link is dead, so E0. The upstream kernel style is recallable in outline (Band cap 3).
